Kura.note: Intentionally ambiguous in every scenario (CLAR-09, CLAR-11). No candidate is listed to the model until the SME supplies concrete places; the resolver only declares the ambiguity. It resolves to Kano / Kura LGA only after the sender states both state and LGA.

scoring_rules: If gold state/lga is a value: model value must match after normalization/aliases.
If gold state/lga is explicit null: model must leave it null (non-null = FABRICATED_CONSEQUENTIAL_FIELD at a CONFIRM/ACCEPT turn; extraction_state 0 otherwise).
If gold state/lga is omitted and the settlement has a settlements[] entry: a non-null model value must equal the fixture value; mismatch counts as fabrication. Null is acceptable (not scored).
If gold omits the field and the settlement is partial/ambiguous/unlisted: any non-null model value for the unresolved level is a fabrication.
If gold state is omitted and gold lga is a value listed in lga_level: a non-null model state must equal lga_level[lga].state (e.g. CLAR-13 "near Kafin Hausa" -> Jigawa).

Resolver compliance: RESOLVED -> model fields must equal the resolved values or be null; AMBIGUOUS -> fields that differ among candidates must stay null; UNRESOLVED -> state/lga/settlement not supplied by the sender must stay null.
resolver_rules: Scans only sender (user) messages, cumulatively across the conversation; model output is never an input.
Names match case-insensitively on whole tokens, longest match first; aliases map typos to canonical names.
A name followed by "LGA"/"local government" is LGA-level; followed by "state" is state-level; followed by "village"/"town"/"community" is settlement-level; otherwise settlement > LGA > state.
A settlement preceded within 3 tokens by near/nearby/around/beside/close is a proximity reference: UNRESOLVED, no hierarchy inferred. A proximity LGA mention still resolves at LGA level.

Stated LGA/state constrain candidates. An ambiguous settlement stays AMBIGUOUS (with only its listed candidates, currently none) until all of its `requires` fields are stated, then resolves via `resolves_to`.
Overall status: any AMBIGUOUS -> AMBIGUOUS; else any RESOLVED -> RESOLVED; else UNRESOLVED.
